newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen drifting sideways or down.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen drifting sideways or down.

text.p: Polish shares fell in lower turnover after Tuesday's rise and analysts saw the market extending falls or drifting sideways as the current price levels were unlikely to stir up substantial buying interest.
The main market's WIG index fell 295.2 points, or 1.8 percent, to 16,462.8, and trade fell 24.3 percent to 136.7 million zlotys ($45.6 million) as 68 issues fell, 13 rose and 10 were flat.

"Big investors don't want to buy at this level and will rather wait for primary market offers and they could start buying on the exchange only if there are more falls...when it becomes cheaper," said Tomasz Berent of IB Austria brokerage.
Analysts said fears of higher U.S. interest rates were also affecting the Polish bourse but good prospects of Poland's economy made the Warsaw market attractive in the long run.
Some analysts said the market might enter a deeper downtrend soon after its 1.5-year growth but said it was hard to say where it would find its support.
Steel products maker Centrostal SA began parallel market trade at 6.5 zlotys ($2.2), 55 percent above issue price.

Construction firm Espebepe tumbled 9.7 percent, extending its two-session fall with no trade after price-fixing for the third consecutive day due to excess supply on growing concern that the company would go bankrupt.
The WIG 20 closed at 1,624.6 points in continuous trade, 0.9 percent lower than at the regular session, in a 40.3-million zloty ($13.4 million) turnover.
